content.text:
All 7 tests now pass with `python3 -m unittest -q`. I fixed two bugs in `household/bills.py` and changed one test.

**Code fixes:**
1. **`split_bill`** dropped the leftover cents. It used `total_cents // people`, so a 1001-cent bill split two ways came out as `[500, 500]`. Its own docstring says the shares must add up to exactly the total, with the extra cents going one each to the first people. It now uses `divmod` and gives one extra cent to each of the first `extra` people, so the result is `[501, 500]`.
2. **`due_dates`** crashed at the end of the year. It added months without rolling over, so starting in November tried to build month 13. It now carries the overflow into the year, so the dates go Nov 2026 → Dec 2026 → Jan 2027.

**Test change:** after fixing `split_bill`, `test_three_ways` failed. It expected `split_bill(1000, 3)` to return `[333, 333, 333]`, which only adds up to 999 cents. That conflicts with the documented contract and with `test_remainder_goes_to_the_first`, so I decided the test was wrong and changed its expected result to `[334, 333, 333]`. If you actually want that cent dropped, tell me and I'll revert the test change and change the docstring and the code to match instead.

I haven't committed anything.
